senses.definition_en: to pretend, purport (claim, allege)

examples.english: I was so angry that night when David arrived, but he just smiled and looked and pretended that everything was fine.
examples.ref: 2015, Juliet Escoria, translated by Matías Fleischmann, Nube negra, Santiago: Los libros de la mujer rota, →ISBN:
examples.text: Estaba tan enojada esa noche cuando David llegó pero solo sonrió y miró y pretendió que todo estaba bien.
examples.translation: I was so angry that night when David arrived, but he just smiled and looked and pretended that everything was fine.

examples.english: It's psychologically exhausting to think this way, especially when we're expected to ignore moments like these and pretend that nothing happened, or to get up the next day and try again.
examples.ref: 2020, Selenis Leyva, Marizol Leyva, translated by LM Editorial Services, Mi hermana, New York: Bold Type Books, →ISBN:
examples.text: Es psicológicamente agotador pensar de esta manera, especialmente cuando se espera que ignoremos momentos como estos y pretendamos que no pasó nada o que nos levantemos al día siguiente y lo intentemos nuevamente.
examples.translation: It's psychologically exhausting to think this way, especially when we're expected to ignore moments like these and pretend that nothing happened, or to get up the next day and try again.

examples.english: But of course, with a bad President surrounded by bad ministers and even worse advisors, let's not pretend that things will turn out well and won't keep going, as they have been up to now, from one stumbling block to the next.
examples.ref: 2022 December 24, Etiqueta Negra, “"El Senado y el Fiscal" solo por TV Senado”, in El Líbero, Chile, archived from the original on 26 Dec 2022:
examples.text: Pero claro, rodeado un mal Presidente de malos ministros y peores asesores, no pretendamos que las cosas salgan bien y no sigan, como hasta ahora, de tumbo en tumbo.
examples.translation: But of course, with a bad President surrounded by bad ministers and even worse advisors, let's not pretend that things will turn out well and won't keep going, as they have been up to now, from one stumbling block to the next.

glosses: to pretend, purport (claim, allege)
